heroHeadline: Pakistan Strikes Dangam, Kunar — 3 Civilians Killed; ISPR Doubles Down: Op Ghazab Continues 'Until Taliban Provides TTP Guarantees'
heroSubtitle: On Day 70 of Operation Ghazab lil-Haq (May 5–6, 2026), Pakistan struck civilian areas in Dangam district, Kunar province, killing 3 and injuring 14 — drawing an Afghan Taliban condemnation as a 'war crime' and new calls for UN Security Council action. Hours later, Pakistan's 275th Corps Commanders' Conference under Field Marshal Asim Munir declared the army was 'in no hurry' to end the operation, citing a 65% reduction in KPK terror incidents and insisting the Taliban must provide credible guarantees to dismantle TTP before operations cease. China — the only active mediator — has not publicly condemned the Dangam strike or called for new talks. The Urumqi Round 2 peace process remains unscheduled, the UK-Pakistan diplomatic rift over civilian casualties deepened, and the UN's formal alarm over 146,000+ Afghan deportations in 2026 reflects a conflict with no off-ramp in sight.
footerNote: Data sourced from UNAMA, SIGAR, ACLED, Brown University Costs of War Project, US DoD, Reuters, BBC, Al Jazeera, Tolo News, Dawn, Geo News, HRW, OHCHR, OCHA
